sources.entry: Fluor - Handy tool for macOS allowing you to switch Fn keys' mode based on active application.

summary.one_liner: Fluor is a macOS menu-bar tool that automatically switches the keyboard's Fn keys between standard Apple function behavior and F1–F12 mode depending on which application is active.
summary.what_it_does: Fluor sits in the macOS status bar and shows which Fn-key mode the keyboard is currently in. Each application can have its own rule, so the Fn keys can act as Apple default function keys or as standard F1, F2, F3 keys when that app is in focus. The menu lets you pick a default mode, see the active application and its rule, change the rule on the fly, or disable Fluor so the keyboard reverts to its prior behavior. A Rules Editor lists, edits, and deletes rules, and adding one opens a file selector to choose an app. A Running Applications panel lets you set rules for any running process, which helps with apps like Steam games that the file selector may not handle. The README says the app is MIT licensed and can be installed from a DMG or via Homebrew Cask.
use_cases: Switch keyboard Fn keys to F1–F12 in specific apps
Keep Apple media/function key behavior in other apps
Set per-application keyboard function key rules on macOS
Run Fluor from the menu bar to change Fn-key mode quickly
Make Fn keys work as standard function keys in games or IDEs
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the project's releases, open the DMG, and drag Fluor to /Applications
Or install via Homebrew Cask: brew cask install fluor
Building from source is possible but the README says it is not recommended for regular use
stack: Objective-C/Swift (macOS app, inferred from source build mention; not named in README)
notable: Per-application rules that switch Fn-key mode automatically
Status bar app with quick default-mode and disable controls
Running Applications panel to set rules for processes that cannot be picked from a file selector
Free and open source, positioned as an alternative to a paid or sandboxed App Store release
caveats: The README is marked out-of-date at the top
The app is non-sandboxed and therefore not on the Mac App Store, per the README
Building from source is discouraged for ordinary users
